title: AgentCoder: Multi-Agent-based Code Generation with Iterative Testing and Optimisation
authors: Dong Huang, Jie M. Zhang, Michael Luck, Qingwen Bu, Yuhao Qing, Heming Cui
abstract-summary: Multi-agent framework with programmer/test-designer/test-executor agents for iterative code generation and testing
notes: SA baseline is GPT-4 direct prompting (67.0%). MA also scored 91.8% on MBPP vs ~52% SA.

title: MapCoder: Multi-Agent Code Generation for Competitive Problem Solving
authors: Md. Ashraful Islam, Mohammed Eunus Ali, Md Rizwan Parvez
abstract-summary: Four-agent pipeline (retrieval/planning/coding/debugging) for competitive programming code generation
notes: Also MBPP 83.1%, APPS 22.0%, CodeContests 28.5%. SA baseline is GPT-4 direct.

title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
authors: Sirui Hong, Mingchen Zhuge, Jonathan Chen, Xiawu Zheng, Yuheng Cheng, et al.
abstract-summary: Multi-agent framework using structured outputs (documents/diagrams) for software development with SOPs
notes: Also 87.7% on MBPP. SA baseline is GPT-4 direct. Agents communicate via structured documents, not dialogue.

title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
authors: Chen Qian, Wei Liu, Hongzhang Liu, Nuo Chen, Yufan Dang, et al.
abstract-summary: Virtual software company with 7 role-playing agents (CEO/CTO/programmer/reviewer/tester/designer/CPO)
notes: Quality score 0.3953 vs MetaGPT 0.1523. Evaluated on software project generation, not function-level benchmarks.

title: SWE-Search: Enhancing Software Agents with Monte Carlo Tree Search and Iterative Refinement
authors: Antonis Antoniades, Albert Örwall, Kexun Zhang, Yuxi Xie, Anirudh Goyal, William Wang
abstract-summary: Multi-agent MCTS with SWE-Agent/Value-Agent/Discriminator-Agent for repo-level issue resolution
notes: 23% relative improvement over baseline across 5 models. Published at ICLR 2025.

title: CodeR: Issue Resolving with Multi-Agent and Task Graphs
authors: Dong Chen, Haowei Tao, Yi Wen, Haiquan Zhao
abstract-summary: Multi-agent framework with fault-localizer/editor/verifier using pre-defined task graphs
notes: Builds on AutoCodeRover search. SA baseline is AutoCodeRover at 19%.

title: MASAI: Modular Architecture for Software-engineering AI Agents
authors: Daman Jain, Abhiram Kothapalli, Naman Jain, et al.
abstract-summary: Modular multi-agent system with specialized sub-agents for SWE tasks at <$2/issue
notes: Achieved state-of-the-art at time of submission. Modular sub-agents with different strategies.

title: AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement
authors: Yuntong Zhang, Haifeng Ruan, Zhiyu Fan, Abhik Roychoudhury
abstract-summary: Program-structure-aware autonomous agent using iterative code search for GitHub issues
notes: Single-agent but structure-aware. Used as SA baseline by CodeR. Cost $0.43/issue.

title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
authors: Chunqiu Steven Xia, Yinlin Deng, Soren Dunn, Lingming Zhang
abstract-summary: Three-phase agentless approach (localize/repair/validate) without autonomous agent decisions
notes: Key SA baseline. No agent loop. Cost $0.70/issue. Adopted by OpenAI/DeepSeek for model eval.

title: Diversity Empowers Intelligence: Integrating Expertise of Software Engineering Agents
authors: Kexun Zhang, Weiran Yao, Zuxin Liu, Yihao Feng, et al.
abstract-summary: Meta-module (DEI) that orchestrates diverse SWE agents via rating and re-ranking pipeline
notes: Best individual agent: 27.3%. DEI ensemble: 34.3% (25% improvement). Best group reaches 55%.

title: Agyn: A Multi-Agent System for Team-Based Autonomous Software Engineering
authors: Nikita Benkovich, Dmitrii Khizbullin
abstract-summary: Multi-agent team (manager/researcher/engineer/reviewer) modeling real engineering org structure
notes: SA baseline ~65% (single GPT-5 agent). 7.2% absolute improvement. Not tuned for SWE-bench.

title: CodeCoR: An LLM-Based Self-Reflective Multi-Agent Framework for Code Generation
authors: Ruwei Pan, Hongyu Zhang, Chao Liu
abstract-summary: Four-agent framework (prompt/code/test/repair) with self-reflection and quality pruning
notes: Avg across HumanEval/HumanEval-ET/MBPP/MBPP-ET. Outperforms MapCoder (72.8% avg). SA baseline is direct prompting.

title: Self-Organized Agents: A LLM Multi-Agent Framework toward Ultra Large-Scale Code Generation and Optimization
authors: Yoichi Ishibashi, Yoshimasa Nishimura
abstract-summary: Dynamic multi-agent framework with automatic agent multiplication based on problem complexity
notes: 5% improvement over Reflexion (strong SA baseline). Scales agent count with problem complexity.

title: CodeTree: Agent-guided Tree Search for Code Generation with Large Language Models
authors: Jierui Li, Hung Le, Zhangming Chan, Yizhi LI
abstract-summary: Multi-agent tree search with Thinker/Solver/Debugger/Critic agents for unified code generation
notes: Also MBPP 98.7%, CodeContests 43.0%, SWE-bench 31.9%. Critic guides tree search.

title: Self-collaboration Code Generation via ChatGPT
authors: Yihong Dong, Xue Jiang, Zhi Jin, Ge Li
abstract-summary: Multi-role self-collaboration framework where one LLM plays analyst/coder/tester roles
notes: 47.1% relative improvement on CoderEval. 29.9-34.6% on HumanEval-ET/MBPP-ET. SA=direct ChatGPT.

title: CodeSIM: Multi-Agent Code Generation and Problem Solving through Simulation-Driven Planning and Debugging
authors: Md. Ashraful Islam, Raian Rahman, Mohammed Eunus Ali, Md Rizwan Parvez
abstract-summary: Simulation-driven multi-agent with planning verification before coding and trace-based debugging
notes: Also MBPP 90.7%, CodeContests 29.1%. Outperforms MapCoder (79.0% avg) by 3.7% absolute.

title: DebateCoder: Adaptive Confidence Gating in Multi-Agent Collaboration for Efficient Code Generation
authors: Yu Xie, et al.
abstract-summary: Three-agent debate (User/Technical/QA) with adaptive confidence gating for small LMs
notes: SA baseline is Pangu-1B direct (28.46%). MBPP: 63.22% MA vs 28.46% SA. Targets SLMs.

title: InfCode: Adversarial Iterative Refinement of Tests and Patches for Reliable Software Issue Resolution
authors: et al.
abstract-summary: Adversarial multi-agent with test-generator/code-patcher/selector for iterative co-refinement
notes: SOTA on SWE-bench Verified (Nov 2025). Surpasses TRAE (78.8%) and Rovo Dev (76.8%). Open-source.

title: RGD: Multi-LLM Based Agent Debugger via Refinement and Generation Guidance
authors: Doki Hollin, et al.
abstract-summary: Three-agent (Guide/Debug/Feedback) debugger with memory pool for generation guidance
notes: 9.8% improvement on HumanEval and 16.2% on MBPP over SOTA. Uses memory pool of successful guides.

title: SWE-Debate: Competitive Multi-Agent Debate for Software Issue Resolution
authors: Yang, et al.
abstract-summary: Competitive multi-agent debate with fault-propagation traces and MCTS-based patch generation
notes: SOTA among open-source agents. Three-round debate among specialized agents. Accepted at ICSE 2026.

title: Blueprint2Code: A Multi-Agent Pipeline for Reliable Code Generation via Blueprint Planning and Repair
authors: Lee, et al.
abstract-summary: Four-agent pipeline (Preview/Blueprint/Coding/Debugging) with blueprint planning
notes: Also MBPP 88.4%. Emulates human programming workflow with detailed blueprint planning step.

title: Lessons Learned: A Multi-Agent Framework for Code LLMs to Learn and Improve
authors: Yuanzhe Liu, Ryan Deng, Tim Kaler, et al.
abstract-summary: Lesson-sharing multi-agent framework where agents learn from each others successes/failures
notes: Team of small LLMs outperforms larger single LLM. NeurIPS 2025. Lesson solicitation-banking-selection.

title: AdaCoder: An Adaptive Planning and Multi-Agent Framework for Function-Level Code Generation
authors: et al.
abstract-summary: Adaptive two-phase framework with rule-based debugging and LLM-based planning agents
notes: 27.69% higher Pass@1 than MapCoder on avg. 16x faster inference, 12x less tokens.

title: Enhancing LLM Code Generation: A Systematic Evaluation of Multi-Agent Collaboration and Runtime Debugging
authors: Nazmus Ashrafi, Salah Bouktif, Mohammed Mediani
abstract-summary: Systematic evaluation of multi-agent collaboration + runtime debugging across 19 LLMs
notes: Evaluates 6 approaches (Basic/AC/ACT/Debug/AC+Debug/ACT+Debug). ACT+Debug best overall.

title: TraceCoder: A Trace-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Debugging of LLM-Generated Code
authors: et al.
abstract-summary: Modular multi-agent debugging framework with runtime trace analysis and historical lesson learning
notes: 34.43% relative improvement over best baseline. Also evaluated on BigCodeBench and HumanEval+.
